AA Prototype · Requirements catch-up

The catch-up: from the RFP to the catalogue

The prototype was built in July against the original RFP, in fourteen phases. The requirements catalogue has since become the source of truth and moved a long way: Bookings instead of Cards, Slots and Draft Lists, one Contract per Procedure locked at authorise, admin-decided hospital matching, an internal ledger with Xero as its mirror. This plan closes every verified gap in 41 further phases, numbered 14 to 44, each one focused session (at most two) with one coherent deliverable, and every automatic or external event given a demo button on the screen where it matters.

What changed since the prototype

The prototype is a sound July-2026 build of the original RFP, but the catalogue has moved well past it. Of roughly 190 graded items, about 40 Match (mostly mobile/web capture, audit, billing-monitor and the per-counterparty invoice grouping), about 70 are Partial, about 40 Contradict and about 35 are Missing. Seven epics (EP-01, EP-04, EP-06, EP-08 late billing, EP-10 fee, EP-11, EP-02 intake) are Contradicts or XL at epic level. The gap is mostly structural, not cosmetic. Four model rewrites carry most of it: Slot/List/Draft List (DM-02, DM-03), Contract-defines-everything (DM-07, DM-10, DM-11), Events plus credit/rebill (DM-17, DM-18, DM-24) and the internal ledger with fee/payable changes (DM-22, DM-26). Two of these (Contract model, intake matching) sit on items still at Verify or Proposed, so build thin.

The themes below are the gap analysis's own grouping. Each lists the phases that carry its items. Full reasoning: GAP-ANALYSIS.md.

  1. Slot, List and Draft List

    Slot and List welded; status is a code enum; cover is an unresolved request marker. Catalogue wants free-by-default Slots, separate Draft List, editable status master, List shown in place of status, and no-acceptance anaesthetist moves to office or colleague. Structural keystone for schedule work. XL.

    26 items · built in phases 28, 29, 30, 31, 32a, 32

  2. Contract replaces the billing route

    Procedure.billingRoute, guardian override and insurerId are the retired model. Contract must carry category, scope, aaCode, versions and payment setting, define the billable party, and be picked once per Procedure. OQ-78 open. XL.

    27 items · built in phases 18, 20, 21, 22, 23, 25

  3. Procedure master, base units on Contracts, default modifiers

    No procedure master; base units on RvgCode; range clamps and blocks; modifiers absorbed. Needs procedure master, default RVG Contracts, free out-of-range entry with office warning, pre-filled default modifiers. OQ-88 first. XL.

    13 items · built in phases 19a, 19, 20

  4. Pricing rule changes

    Hourly rate x time becomes Contract unit rate (OQ-89); modifier split above 4 units; anaesthetist adjustment gated by Contract; fee-schedule lines; tiers as data. L.

    15 items · built in phases 24, 19a, 39b, 18, 23

  5. Events, additional invoices, credit and rebill

    Post-op addendum Booking replaced by an Event on the Procedure with invoice tick and review step; admin additional invoice; credit in full then rebill; negative payable netted in payment run. One build. XL.

    17 items · built in phases 39b, 38b, 39, 39a

  6. Prepayment re-founded

    Trigger from anaesthetist prepaid RVG set; automatic all-or-nothing estimate with contingency and estimated duration; trust hold, refund on cancel, payable repoint on move; overpay no longer fails the Booking. XL.

    21 items · built in phases 27, 41, 32a, 26

  7. Money model: AA fee, payables, ledger, GST, Xero

    5% netted fee becomes a monthly fee invoice (OQ-60); ACCPAY equals receivable; ledger evolution and AUTHORISED snapshot; ageing removed; GST on disbursed payables; patient name out of Xero contacts. L.

    21 items · built in phases 16, 39a, 22, 25, 36, 38, 39

  8. Intake becomes an admin matching screen

    Hospital rows must stage in an Admin queue with match/create/create-Draft/reject; nothing applies silently; explicit Save, change sets, update email and templates. HL7/FHIR monitor, PDF ingest and automated changes are Future. XL.

    18 items · built in phases 33, 34, 35

  9. Warnings, notifications and admin oversight

    Wire the existing 15a warning routine into to-do list, Day grid and Booking rows; add rules; shared notification pool; ledger and patient balance views; NHI problem list. L.

    19 items · built in phases 15a, 21, 31, 32, 36, 37, 40

  10. Surgeon, rooms, blacklist and master-data editing

    Rooms, surgeon profiles, blacklist, hospital contact emails, spreadsheet loader, master holiday calendar, PWA sign-in. Unlocks update email and blacklist warnings. L.

    13 items · built in phases 17, 32, 42, 43a, 26

  11. Removals and hide-from-demo

    Copy Booking, photo capture, Surgeon PDF tab, dashboard Productivity/Leave panels, ACC review flag, stale open-question copy. S to M.

    7 items · built in phases 15, 18, 34, 38, 44, 15b

How this works

  1. Get the owner decisions first. D1 to D11 (the table at the top of ROADMAP.md) each gate one phase. A phase whose answer has not come in builds the stated default and labels it provisional.
  2. Pick the next phase from the table below, respecting the order in "Sequencing and rules". The Contracts track (17 to 25) and the Schedule track (28 to 32) each run strictly in order.
  3. Open a fresh Claude Code session and paste that phase's kick-off prompt. The agent reads the roadmap, its phase doc, the gap detail for its items, the prototype maps and PROGRESS.md before touching anything.
  4. Drift check first. The catalogue keeps moving. Each session diffs its items against 3d3a18c, reports what changed, and adapts the plan before building.
  5. The agent plans and builds straight on. It turns the phase doc into work-sized steps and starts building without waiting for approval, so phases can run back to back (ROADMAP.md "Owner review: agents test themselves").
  6. Every phase ends the same way: npm run build, npm run build:pwa, npx vitest run and (for UI work) npm run shots green; the checklist run and reported item by item; the adversarial review-and-fix pass (PROGRESS convention 18); the demo guide patched for any beat it broke; the catalogue screenshots brought in step with the app (the phase's capture recipes created or updated, then a full npm run capture in requirements-board/ with no failed recipe and npm run verify:board green, PROGRESS convention 19); a PROGRESS.md entry. Agents never commit.
  7. When the catalogue changes, follow README.md: re-grade the changed items, merge them into gaps.json, update the affected phase docs, and re-render this page with node docs/prototype-build/catch-up/tools/build-index.mjs.

Demo buttons live on their screens. Anything that cannot be shown through normal use (scheduled jobs, backend events, external systems) gets a trigger in the harness bar's "Demo actions" menu, listed only on the screen where it matters. The installed PWA has no harness bar, so it gets the same list as a badged demo-actions sheet, plus office stand-ins for beats that wait on the office. Phase 14 builds the mechanism; every later phase registers into it.

The checklists are the contract. Each phase ends with a short manual test checklist. The agent runs it itself in the running app and reports each item with evidence; nothing is handed to the owner per phase. Each PROGRESS entry ends with a "For the owner's review" list, and Phase 44 gathers them into one list for a single review once every catch-up phase is done.

Sequencing and rules

Owner decisions. D1 to D8 and D10 were answered at the 2026-10-01 meeting with Greg, and D12 to D25 (OQ-62 to OQ-75) at the three 2026-10-02 meetings (table at the top of ROADMAP.md). Their phases build the answer, not a default: D1 monthly AA fee invoice from settings (16), D2 insurer and funding source on neither Booking nor Patient (20), D3 any base units with an after-procedure office warning (19), D4 child billable party a mild warning (21), D5 no prepayment gate, a warning in both apps (15a, 27), D6 prepayment invoice generated at setup and sent on admin approval (27), D7 anaesthetist moves their own List with no confirmation (32), D8 flat outstanding list (38), D10 free-form additional invoice (38b), D12 base units in each procedure's default RVG Contracts, the procedure list holding none (19, 19a), D13 'event' as one element on the Procedure with one review step (38b, 39b), D14 Slots as stored status containers with user-maintained statuses, no 'slot' in the UI, and return-or-assign when a booked Slot is marked unavailable (28 to 32), D15 the shared notification pool (32, 35), D16 a short AA code and a picker filtered by procedure then hospital (18, 19a scopes Contracts to procedures, 20), D17 the Contract always defines the billable party (21), D18 typed $ or % split shares set on the Booking (22), D19 an on-demand update email picked from the change history (35), D20 a moved prepaid Booking keeps the agreed amount and only the payable half moves (27, 32a, 41), D21 a negative invoice with no later payment is handled outside the system (39a), D22 additional invoices to any party (38b) with a credit note option (39), D23 prepayment only for a person paying for the patient (27), D24 the balance threshold counts from the invoice date and a credit balance is mild (40), D25 part intervals always round up (19a, 27). D9 billed Lists (38) and D11 Booking without NHI (40) are still open: build the default, label it provisional, and confirm at the drift check. Open questions with a recommendation (OQ-77 to OQ-89 among them) are built as that recommendation, labelled provisional and kept in one place (the meeting's working rule).

Order. 14 and 15 are built. 15a (warnings) is in progress: session 1 (the routine, settings, clearances and the gate removal) is committed and frozen; session 2 builds the surfaces with no submit confirm step. 15a runs before 19, 21, 27 and 40, which register warning rules. 15b (Copy and photo capture out) runs straight after 15a and before 16, so the first milestone (after 16) has the warnings and the removals; 16 re-greens fee removal as step 1 before the monthly fee invoice. The Contracts track runs strictly in order, 17, 18, 19, 19a, 20 to 25: 18 keeps today's resolver and models Contract scope; 19 (RVG, modifier and procedure masters, default modifiers, procedure-first picker) and 19a (default RVG Contracts hold the base units, every Contract scoped to its master procedures, time tiers as data) come straight after 18 so the base-unit source and the procedure scope are final before 20's Contract picker filters by procedure, 23's Booking-level engine and 25's lock; 20 leaves two interims (payer is the Contract holder until 21 captures the Contract-defined billable party; funderOverride stays the split until 22's payment setting); 23 builds the combination Contracts 39 needs; 24 prices whole Procedures at the Contract defined unit rate in place of the hourly line, through one rate function that 39b's UNIT x RATE line later calls (24 builds no billing line), and adds the adjustment; 25 locks what 18 to 24 built, including the base-unit source, the defined rate, the adjustment and the payee. 26 and 27 run back to back after 25; 20's office-set prepayment flag is the interim until 27. 27 also makes a prepaid amount above the final bill cleanly (no invoice, no failure, the excess recorded), because its full estimate plus contingency units is usually above the final and every prepaid Booking would otherwise fail billing until 41; 41 builds the overpaid surfaces and wording. The Schedule track runs strictly in order, 28 to 32a: 31, 32 and 32a reuse 17's blacklist helper; 32 also needs 31 (a List returned to the office becomes a Draft List) and 27 (a move re-checks the prepayment) and builds the notification pool that 35 reads; 32a extends 32's move helpers to a single Booking. Intake 33 to 35 runs after 31 and 20; 34 needs only 33 now that surgeon PDF ingest is Future Work; 35 also needs 25 and 32. 36 runs after 16, 22, 25 and 27; then 37, 38 and 38b in any order; 39 after 23 and 38b (credits are events on 38b's element); 39a after 37 and 39; 38a after 38; 39b after 24, 38a and 38b (it adds pre-op and post-op kinds to the element 38b builds), and soon after 38b, which withdraws the anaesthetist's post-op Card flow: it needs nothing from 39 or 39a, so it may run straight after 38b. 40 after 15a, 34, 36 and 39 (a patient credit balance needs 39's credit notes); 40a after 26 and 40; 41 after 27, 32a (the moved prepaid Booking's payable half is repointed here, for List and single-Booking moves), 39 and 39a; 42 after every master-data phase (17, 18, 19, 19a, 29, 30); 43 after 34, 36, 37 and 42; 43a after 21, 24, 31 and 39b; 44 last. Contracts and Schedule are independent from 17 until 32; Contracts go first because they are mostly Confirmed and carry the S3 to S5 money beats.

Vocabulary. Booking, not Card; move or reassign, never swap; never 'timesheet'. Per OQ-64, 'slot' never reaches app copy (say session, AM or PM); Slot stays a code and planning word. 'Draft List' is kept. 'Event' is the one name for everything recorded against a Procedure after setup; keep its user-facing label in one place (38b), because Greg was unconvinced by it.

BCTI granularity (provisional, one place). The catalogue says both 'one BCTI per procedure' (US-09.1.4 note, OQ-29, note #41) and 'the same value as its receivable' (OQ-42), and a receivable can hold several Procedures, so both cannot hold (DM-22 says so). The plan builds one BCTI, the ACCPAY, per receivable invoice, the same value: the transcript's 'per transaction' (B L71-81), which US-10.2.1's release needs. 16 counts BCTIs for the fee run through one pure, tested function, each once against the anaesthetist who did it and, per Greg's 2026-10-02 view for the accountant, only once paid, both switchable there; 22 (Split gives two invoices, so two BCTIs), 36 (the ledger's payable legs, with a parity test), 38b (additional invoices), 39 (re-issued invoices; whether a credit note or negative invoice counts is OQ-60) and 39b (event invoices) feed it and keep it the only count. 'One per procedure' stays an open point to raise with AA's accountant beside OQ-29 and OQ-60; if it flips, the count function, the $700 seed and the S3 and S4 figures are re-baselined in one place.

Demo triggers. 14 re-homed every existing Control Panel trigger onto its screen and added useDemoTriggerContext for state outside the URL; later phases register or re-point entries, never add to the Control Panel page, which is the index (scenario jumps, clock, reset). Entries declare routes, surfaces (bar, PWA, both), run(api, ctx) on the entity in the URL or the published context, and a disabled state; bodies live in src/shared or src/store for pwaPurity. 15a's 'Raise sample warnings' is shared: each phase that adds a warning rule adds its sample. PWA parity: every beat whose mobile side waits on the office, a colleague or a backend event gets a PWA-only stand-in on that mobile screen (listed per phase, including 32's and 32a's colleague moves and 43a's Sign out); 'Play the office' defaults OFF with a badge, replaced by 14's per-List 'Office authorises this List'; 44 audits parity beat by beat.

Demo guide. Each phase patches the beats it breaks in docs/demo-guide, the same sections of master-demo-guide.html and the Control Panel scenario text, in the same session. Milestone phases (16, 25, 27, 32a, 35, 39a) end with a consistency read of the master guide. 14 added an interim Future-scope caveat to S1; 15a turns S4 Beat 1's gate into a warning with no confirm step; 15b drops the Copy lines; 34 rebuilds S1; 38b turns S4 Beat 2's post-op addendum into an additional invoice and 39 adds a credit-and-rebill beat; 44 rewrites S1 to S5 and regenerates the master guide in full.

Every phase opens with a drift check against 3d3a18c and closes with npm run build, npm run build:pwa, npx vitest run, and npm run shots (Playwright) for any phase touching UI, all green; the adversarial review pass (PROGRESS convention 18); the catalogue screenshot step (recipes, a full npm run capture, npm run verify:board); PERSIST_VERSION bumped on seed changes; Decisions-log entries where a ruling is superseded (route model, 5% fee netting, Copy as an additional procedure and then Phase 15's skeleton Copy, absorbed P1 modifiers, the Method 3 hourly rate line, the guardian override record, the addendum Card, the prepayment completion gate, the overpaid prepayment's negativeTotal failure, the silent BTM fallback, availability reconciliation's conflict flag, office write-through per tap, the cover-request flow, hospital auto-apply, Surgeon PDFs kept in scope by Phase 14); a PROGRESS entry with its 'For the owner's review' list.

Critic points on this update. Followed: the prepaid-excess path back in 27 with US-06.2.3 (41 keeps the surfaces); 39 split, with 38b taking the event element, its review step and the events list as suggested, plus the additional invoice so 38b has a demoable deliverable of its own rather than an empty list; one admin-editable threshold in 40; 'Open in Review' in 37's monitor, with approval kept on Review and logged for the owner; Contract procedure scope given to 19a (not 19, which is full, or 20, which is XL); 39 added to 40's depends and 32a to 41's; the defined rate's whole-Procedure pricing in 24 and the UNIT x RATE line in 39b only. Earlier notes kept. Critic points not followed (first plan): the escalating unpaid-prepayment warning (US-06.3.2) and the re-check (US-06.3.5) stay in 27, not 41, so S4 Beat 1 keeps a control; US-04.2.2 closes in 24, not 23, because its last missing parts are Contract rules (the allows-adjustment rule and now the defined rate). Second review: Phase 32 keeps its file name and slug (phase-32-swap-requests), because the plan tools pin an existing phase's doc path in plan.json; the title and all app-facing copy say 'move'. Phase 39 keeps its file name (phase-39-additional-invoices-and-credit) for the same reason. 2026-10-01 update: 15a early; US-05.5.2 and US-03.3.6 in 39b; US-08.6.4 unparked into 39; FT-06.4 and US-06.4.2 in 41; US-09.3.1 in 16; US-15.0.1 in its own late phase (43a); 32 as the anaesthetist's own move; the moved prepaid Booking's payee repoint (US-06.5.4) in 41. The plan totals about 69 sessions over 41 phases.

14

Screen-contextual demo triggers

Foundations Start here 2 sessions plan doc ↗ 1 item covered

Build one shared, pure trigger registry in src/shared/demoTriggers (its own index, modelled on demoClockShortcuts, not re-exported from the shared component barrel), plus a small useDemoTriggerContext hook for screen state the URL cannot carry, such as the Admin Integrations tab and the simulator's selected message. Each entry declares its route patterns, where it shows (harness bar, PWA sheet or both), a run(api, ctx) that acts on the entity in the URL or on the published state, a disabled reason, and an index link with an optional hint. The harness bar gets one 'Demo actions' pill that lists only the current screen's triggers and is hidden when there are none. The PWA gets the same list as a badged bottom sheet. Every Control Panel trigger moves to its own screen, except 'Run payables', whose home is the Billing monitor's existing product button. The Control Panel becomes the index, keeping scenario jumps, clock and reset. FT-13.5 gets a 'Simulate sign-in attempts' trigger on Admin Audit that writes five audit rows. 'Play the office' is off by default, badged when on, and replaced in the story by a per-List 'Office authorises this List'. The HL7/FHIR tooling gets interim Future-scope badges, and S1 gets a caveat.

FT-13.5board
Demo triggers and risks
  • Admin Audit: 'Simulate sign-in attempts' (an Admin sign-in with MFA, a failed attempt, an anaesthetist self-service password reset)
  • Admin Billing monitor: 'Trigger billing failure', 'Arm handoff failure', 'Run payables', 'Run reconciliation poll', 'Run archive job' (re-homed from the Control Panel)
  • Admin Review, on Dr Sharma's Tue 14 Jul List: 'Stage post-op scenario' (re-homed)
  • Admin Integrations, Surgeon PDFs tab (read through the context hook): 'Ingest PDF row' (re-homed)
  • Admin invoice document and Xero pair detail: 'Payment received (webhook)' Full or Half, and 'Replay last event', for the invoice in the URL (re-homed)
  • Xero sim: 'Run reconciliation poll', 'Run archive job' (re-homed)
  • Integrations simulator, Admin Integrations and mobile Lists: 'Fire hospital message' and 'Replay last (dedupe)', badged Future scope (re-homed; S1 fires it from the mobile screen)
  • PWA sheet, mobile List: 'Office authorises this List' (so 'Play the office' can default OFF, badged when on)
  • PWA sheet, mobile Balances: 'Payment received' Full or Half on an open invoice

Risks. pwaPurity.test forbids shell or demo imports in the PWA closure, so the registry, the context hook, trigger bodies and shared OFFICE and SOUTER actor constants live in src/shared or src/store. The 48px bar has no responsive handling: one menu pill, not many buttons. Office stand-ins declare the PWA surface only, because in the framed build the presenter plays the office in Admin. Playwright data-shot hooks (control-payment-webhook, control-scheduled-jobs, control-integration-message) move with their triggers, so the specs change here. Re-home first and re-green, then add the new pieces.

What to check when it's done
  • The harness bar shows no 'Demo actions' pill on the Admin Day view. On the Billing monitor it lists exactly four entries. Every Control Panel 'Open screen' link, with its hint where shown, lands on a screen whose menu contains that entry, and no trigger buttons remain on the Control Panel.
  • Each re-homed trigger behaves exactly as its Control Panel card did: same store calls, actors, guards and idempotency keys, and half-payment falls back to the full amount when half rounds to 0. 'Ingest PDF row' appears only on the Surgeon PDFs tab. Replay after a reset refuses cleanly.
  • Installed PWA with fresh or corrupt storage: 'Play the office' is OFF and a submitted List waits. The Demo chip on that List runs 'Office authorises this List', which authorises and bills it. Balances takes a chosen payment. pwaPurity.test stays green, with the bar menu forbidden.
  • 'Simulate sign-in attempts' adds five labelled audit rows through mutate() only: provisioning, Admin sign-in with MFA, failed sign-in, self-service reset and mobile social login. Future-scope badges show on the simulator and on the Messages and Feed config tabs. The S1 caveat is in place. build, build:pwa, vitest, shots and verify:board are all green, and the 4 specs, 18 recipes and ATLAS are updated.

The insurer member number is a required-input value only.

Remove never promotes. Make primary is one commit with two audit entries, it moves the Booking's modifier inputs to the new primary, clears the old primary's base inputs, and the new primary moves to the top. editProcedure refuses base and modifier values on an additional Procedure, and any isPrimary patch, but still allows clearing those keys, because a procedure or code change sends them as undefined; 19's pickProcedure and 20's Contract pick seed no base input on an additional Procedure, and its default modifiers join the primary's set, add-only. An added Procedure starts on the primary's Contract.

Contracts After phase 23 2 sessions plan doc ↗ 11 items covered

Session 1 replaces the hourly rate x time line, its Method 3 flag, permitsRateTime and the validator gate with a Contract defined unit rate. It is built as OQ-89 recommends and labelled provisional in one place: the agreed rate per unit, pricing the whole Procedure through one pure unitRateFor function, which 39b's UNIT x RATE line will also call. No billing line is added. The Aria Contract keeps the id CT-ARIA-HOURLY, gets $26.50 per unit, and Fitzgerald's Booking re-prices at (B+T+M) x $26.50. Review, the admin total and the invoice show both layers. The anaesthetist sees no fee or rate.

While working:

The HPI CPN stays the one hpiId field, labelled "HPI CPN" everywhere (no "HPI id" or "HPI number"), checked with Phase 17's normaliseHpiCpn, isPlausibleHpiCpn and duplicate check. The GST number is Phase 22's field and validator; reuse them.
- Nothing is derived from the prepaid set in this phase. No Booking, banner, gate or review flag reads prepaidSettings; Phase 20's office-set Booking prepayment flag and bookingRequiresPrepayment (Phase 15's name for cardRequiresPrepayment) stay untouched. Phase 27 does the derivation.
- Build the pure helpers first, with Vitest tests: bank account normalise and mask, the prepaid set (normalise, validate, expand, reason, summary) on Phase 19's codesInGroup, and the profile field policy as data.
- Permissions are enforced in the store. The anaesthetist edits only their own rate, GST period, GST number, contact details and prepaid set. The office edits everything, including bank details, the HPI CPN and active. Nobody edits the registration number. Any role 'system' actor (integration feeds, runs, demo control) edits nothing. Refusals render verbatim.
- Every write goes through mutate() and is audited. Office edits carry onBehalfOf (MutationMeta gains it and mutate() copies it onto the AuditEntry). Bank numbers are masked in the audit and everywhere outside the office's edit field. A no-change save writes no audit entry.
- Group and AA-code deletes are refused while an anaesthetist's prepaid set references them.
- Bank details are display-only (DM-33). The payables run shows each destination account (or a warning-tone "No bank account on file") and snapshots it on the disbursement; it holds, reroutes or re-amounts nothing. No seeded payout changes.
- A GST number edit never changes an invoice already issued (Phase 22's supplier snapshot).
- Mock backend only. Determinism: seeded bank numbers are built from the registration number on non-issued bank code 99, and nothing new draws from the seeded RNG. Bump PERSIST_VERSION once.
- Keep the seed coherent for Phase 27: the seeded prepaid sets, counted only where the Procedure's effective billable party is a person paying for the patient (Phase 21's billablePartyForProcedure passing isPersonParty; US-06.2.1 as changed at 3d3a18c and OQ-73's recommendation, which Phase 27 builds), must hit exactly the Bookings Phase 20 flagged for prepayment (Nair on 41800, not 41789), with Riley's uncoded Booking as the one noted exception. Change a seeded set, never a Booking's code.
- The shared tick list and profile rows live in src/shared/profile and import nothing from apps/, so pwaPurity stays green.
- Design: mobile edits in bottom sheets with a sticky teal Save, never a desktop form. The web profile is a desktop layout reached from the persona block, and the four nav tabs are unchanged. Teal is the only action colour, crimson is identity only, and "via" and "Not on file" markers are neutral or warning-tone pills. Money and account numbers are mono.
- No en dashes or em dashes in any app-facing copy.
- Demo triggers: none. Everything is normal use, so add no trigger-registry entry, no 15a warning sample, and leave the Control Panel alone.
- Build nothing ahead of the plan: no prepayment derivation, estimator, GST schedule rework, payout history, payout hold, bank verification, HPI CPN register lookup or check character (no phase builds them; 40a only unifies the label and format), start date (28) or notifications.
- Keep npm run build, npm run build:pwa and npx vitest run green at the end of the session.

- Run npm run build, npm run build:pwa, npx vitest run, npm run shots and npm run verify:board, all green, with no S1 to S5 figure moved and PERSIST_VERSION bumped once.

- Update PROGRESS.md: status row, phase entry with the drift-check result, the review pass and the catalogue screenshot result (REPORT.md counts before and after), the Decisions-log entries listed in the phase doc, and the handoff notes for 27, 28, 36, 37, 38, 40a and 42.

Phase goal: give each anaesthetist a profile they own on mobile and web (rate per unit, GST period, GST number, contact details, a read-only HPI CPN, a masked, display-only bank account and a prepaid tick list of RVG codes and groups), let the office maintain it on their behalf with every edit audited (including the HPI CPN, format-checked), and show the destination account on the payables run, ready for Phase 27 to derive prepayment from the stored set.

Demo triggers and risks
  • Admin Day: 'Move to 2 days before procedure' (a demo clock jump that turns the unpaid-prepayment warning from mild to strong)
  • Admin Day and Booking detail: 'Add prepaid-list Booking' (creates a Booking matching Dr Souter's prepaid set on her next open List, so its invoice appears 'Awaiting approval')
  • Booking detail and Admin Invoices: 'Approve and send' on a generated prepayment invoice (product)
  • Re-homed 'Payment received (webhook)' Half on the prepayment invoice shows part-paid
  • PWA sheet, mobile Booking: 'Office approves and sends the prepayment invoice'

Risks. The gate is already gone (15a); this phase adds derivation, the approval step, the excess path and escalation. Without the excess path every prepaid Booking authorised from here on would fail billing with negativeTotal, S4 Beat 1 included, so it lands in this phase: leave it unseeded (no seeded Booking is prepaid above its final; a seed test pins that) and cover it in the manual test. EP-06, US-06.2.2, US-06.3.1 and US-06.3.5 are Verify. The contingency buffer is OQ-38 (two units as a setting, shown in the estimate, not recorded as modifiers); whether a prepayment is ever partial is OQ-76 (build all or nothing); when the pair is created and amended is OQ-80 (build its recommendation). S4 Beat 1 (Riley, Nair) is rewritten here around generate, approve and send. This builds on billing cases that Phase 36 promotes. The estimated-duration field added here is entered by the office; surgeon PDF ingest is Future Work. Letters, the balance invoice's citation of the prepayment and its 'prepayment' wording, the overpaid case's surfaces and its 'Stage overpaid prepayment' beat, the trust hold, refunds and the moved-Booking payee are Phase 41.

- The estimator is pure, in src/domain/billing, with Vitest tests: base units from the Procedure's Contract, the procedure's default RVG Contract unless another Contract or a Contract base-unit override applies (OQ-62, US-04.4.2), through Phase 19's resolveBaseUnits with the contractBaseUnits 19a's lookup supplies (called directly, not through resolveBtm or feeFor, and never the RVG reference value directly), with a prepaid additional Procedure estimated as Phase 23 will charge it (no base units under an rvgDefault rule; see work item 3 and check how 23 shipped), time units from each Procedure's own estimated duration through the same tiered function and rule as the final (19a's timeUnitsFromMinutes(minutes, rule) with masters.rvgTimeRule; every part interval rounded up, D25: 95 minutes is 7 units, 125 is 9; no time-rule caveat), contingency units from appSettings (never a literal 2; the one "Provisional (OQ-38)" caption), all at the anaesthetist's own unit value. The AC figure (10 base + 90 minutes = 18 units) is exact. The amount is stored on the Booking, ex-GST, with its breakdown.
- One engine routine, syncPrepayment, is the only writer of the stored estimate and the only generator of the prepayment invoice. It runs as the engine after every listed action (booking setup, procedure, Contract, payer and duration changes, the setting, cancel, every move, unit value and prepaid-set edits; Copy is gone since 15b), audits with its cause (a PrepaymentSyncCause union that includes listMoved and bookingMoved for Phases 28, 31, 32 and 32a; Phase 32's plan may call the routine recheckPrepayment, so record the shipped name in the handoff), returns its outcome for a one-line "Pre-payment re-checked" confirmation, and is idempotent. A generated invoice is held "Awaiting approval" with its draft Xero pair, created at generation and only in generatePrepaymentInvoice (OQ-80's recommendation, provisional, one comment), never emailed or payable; a held invoice is re-estimated in place or withdrawn; a sent invoice is never rewritten, and a move after sending keeps the agreed amount and raises no new invoice (D20; "agreed" means sent, a reading to log). The payable half's update to the doer is Phase 41's. List submit never invoices it again; a held invoice at authorise is withdrawn, not netted.
- Approve and send is office only: it sends through Phase 22's delivery plan and moves the ACCREC from draft to awaiting payment. The letter is Phase 41's.
- Status (estimate needed, awaiting approval, unpaid, part paid, paid, no longer needed) and 15a's prepayment warning read mirror money and the demo clock only. No Date.now(), new Date() or Math.random(). The warning is mild from 7 days out and strong from 2 days out (rule params), re-opens at strong after a mild clear, is visible on opening the Booking, and never blocks anything; submit has no confirm step (US-13.7.3).
- The prepaid excess lands here (US-06.2.3, re-graded Contradicts: a lower final fails the Booking today). The full estimate plus contingency is usually above the final, so a group that goes negative only because of prepayment raises no invoice and no failure, its siblings bill, and excessAboveFinal is recorded and audited (OQ-03: not refunded or credited); any other negative group still fails with negativeTotal. Leave it unseeded (a seed test pins every seeded prepaid balance at zero or above) and cover it in the manual test. The deduction line loses "deposit"; the balance invoice's citation of the prepayment invoice (US-06.4.1) and the overpaid case's chip, monitor line, wording and "Stage overpaid prepayment" beat are Phase 41's, so do not build them.
- Every mutation goes through mutate() with audit.
- Keep the filler generator's rng() draw order unchanged and bump PERSIST_VERSION by one. The only seeded prepaid Bookings on open Lists are Riley and Nair, no seeded invoice is awaiting approval, and no seeded prepayment exceeds its final fee.
- Mobile uses bottom sheets, web and admin use inline editors or dialogs, and teal is the only action colour. Crimson never appears on the panel, rail card, approval strip or warning. Amounts are in mono with tabular-nums. No en or em dashes in app copy.
- ENGINE_ACTOR, Invoice.approval, the draft ACCREC status and BillingCase.excessAboveFinal are new in this phase; derivation reuses Phase 26's expandPrepaidCodes and prepaidReasonFor rather than re-expanding groups, and the warning reuses 15a's rule and routine rather than a second alert.
- Demo triggers go in the Phase 14 registry only, never on the Control Panel page. The bar gets "Move to 2 days before procedure" and "Add prepaid-list Booking" on Admin Day and Admin Booking detail, and the re-pointed payment half and full entries. The PWA gets the office stand-in "Office approves and sends the prepayment invoice", "Patient pays half / full of the pre-payment" and the clock jump on the mobile Booking. Re-point 15a's prepayment warning sample at the prepaid set. Bodies live in src/shared or src/store (the stand-in beside authoriseAsSimulatedOffice in src/store/officeStandIn.ts) so pwaPurity passes.

Phase goal: prepayment is derived from the anaesthetist's prepaid list where a person pays for the patient, never an organisation; estimated in full from the default RVG Contract's base units, each Procedure's estimated duration rounded up by the RVG tiers and the contingency setting, stored on the Booking and worded as an estimate; generated as an invoice with its draft pair at setup and sent on admin approval; tracked as unpaid, part paid or paid with a warning in both apps that strengthens as the date approaches; re-checked when the Booking changes or moves, a move keeping the agreed amount; and billed cleanly at authorise, a top-up as the balance or a prepaid amount above the final accepted with no invoice and no failure.
28

Slot and List split

Schedule After phases 14, 15 2 sessions plan doc ↗ 11 items covered

Split the canvas into Slots and Lists. Every active anaesthetist gets an AM and a PM Slot each day, from their start date to a configurable horizon (4 months). Generation writes every Slot free, then paints the anaesthetist's calendar, then the recurring bookings, with no RNG fill. A clash is traced for Phase 31. Availability is a status on the Slot (one mechanism). A List has its own id and slotId, is created only by office assignment (surgeon and hospital required) or by projection, and shows in place of the status. One pure displayStatusKey(slot, list) never reads Bookings and is shared by all three apps and the finders. The Admin roster comes from the anaesthetist master. Default times and the horizon live in one appSettings.schedule record. Reassign moves a List between Slots intact, and the vacated Slot is free by default (OQ-84, provisional). DRAFT reads "Open", the UI never says "slot", and PERSIST_VERSION is bumped.

Risks. The largest structural change on the schedule side: listForSlot and bookingsForList have callers everywhere, including re-homed triggers. Removing the RNG fill empties much of the canvas: seed recurring bookings and Lists so the Day grid and S2 stay demo-plausible, and keep the six-colour design language by deriving the display key from the List. The status values, labels and colours become master data in Phase 29: keep the keys behind one lookup. A long horizon at full scale is Phase 43's concern. Re-walk S2 Beats 1 to 3; a vacated Slot now defaults to free. 'Slot' stays a code and planning word only.

Phase goal: the canvas becomes Slots and Lists. Every active anaesthetist has an AM and a PM Slot per day from their start date to the end of a configurable horizon (four months), written free and then painted with their calendar and the surgeons' recurring bookings, with no invented sessions; the status on the Slot is the one mechanism, with no record reconciled into Lists. A List is created only when the office assigns one (or a recurring booking projects it) and then shows in place of the status. Components never own domain state. setAvailabilityRange, clearAvailability, createAvailabilitySeries and deleteAvailabilitySeries are each one mutate(), all or nothing on refusal, with one audit entry plus one entry per List affected.
- One mechanism (OQ-27 and OQ-64 answered): the calendar writes the Slot's own status directly. A series is a rule (weekdays, sessions, every 1 to 4 weeks, start, optional until) plus exceptions; it writes its Slots, and a single-instance edit or delete is stored as an exception so no later series write, clock roll forward or horizon extend overwrites it. Nothing reads availability from anywhere but Slots. A series fills only Slots at the default status and in no other series, and reports the rest as left as they are. One helper, seriesCalendarFor, feeds active series (with their exceptions) into 28's generateCanvasForDates as calendar input on every generating path (rollCanvasForward, setHorizonMonths when extending, an earlier start date or a reactivation), so they are painted with the anaesthetist's calendar BEFORE recurring bookings (OQ-81 part 1, settled). A recurring booking on a series-closed session is then never placed: 28's generator returns it as a RecurringClash, which Phase 31 turns into a Draft List. The generator's closed test reads isClosed over the status records; it still draws no RNG. Series rules live in src/domain/availabilitySeries.ts, pure and tested.
- The Slot status set becomes a user-maintained master list (masters.slotStatuses, US-01.2.2), availability values only. Each status has a fixed internal ID (SlotStatusKey) that rules read, never its label; seeded IDs are 28's stored values (free, holiday, unavailable), and an added status gets a generated ST#### ID, shown read only and never edited. Label, long label, description, colour (one of the six design tokens) and treatment are editable, plus "open for bookings" and "anaesthetists can set". Seed the owner's starting set: Free (default, dashed), Holiday (long label "On holiday") and Unavailable (hatched), with today's colours. No "available for emergency" and no extra kinds of unavailable seeded; an admin can add them (Greg: several kinds of unavailable, same effect). A rename or recolour shows in every view with every rule unchanged, and an added status works with no code change (US-01.2.2's two criteria; test both). No provisional line anywhere.
- The List types (private, public, pre-op) stay a fixed List attribute with their own tokens, so a session holding a List shows the List in its place with the design's List colours; no status ID can equal a List kind. Log on the "For the owner's review" list that the catalogue has no List kind.
- The only closed sets left are the palette (the six Design Language status tokens in src/theme/statusColours.ts, same hexes) and the List types. No new hex anywhere. The hatched and dashed treatments generalise with tokens only, and today's exact strings must still come out for the seeded statuses and every List.
- No literal availability keys outside src/domain/slotStatus.ts and the seed. Finders, filters, counts and clashes use isOpenForBooking, isClosed and isOpenSlot.
- Availability is never merged into the List. A List in a Slot shows in place of the status. The clash comes from one pure function, availabilityClash: a bookable status clears that List's availability conflict and raises nothing; a closed status over a List flags it once, replacing rather than stacking, with the List's surgeon, hospital, Bookings, times and List type untouched. That flag is the interim for one settled rule, Phase 32's return-or-assign (US-01.5.5) when an anaesthetist marks a session holding a List unavailable; its doc comment says so, and says generation never reaches it (a recurring booking on a closed session is traced as 28's clash for Phase 31's Draft List, not placed and flagged). Warn inline before confirm and never disable it. 28's slotNotAvailable refusal goes, and moveListToSlot stops refusing a closed target (it still refuses an occupied one); the reassign picker keeps open Slots first and adds a collapsed "Not available" group.
- A conflict is only what the catalogue keeps at 3d3a18c: a List at a closed hospital, or a List (and its Bookings) in a session already marked unavailable. A recurring booking landing on an unavailable session is not a conflict: the projection and generator skip it and report it as skipped, and Phase 31 turns it into a Draft List. The writes are create, assign, re-date and remove for Draft Lists, the recurring clash, Bookings added to and moved off them through the existing Booking actions, and the pairing refusals.
- A Draft List is a List record with no anaesthetist and no Slot, plus a draft trail (origin, source, since, by, and for a recurring clash the day it stands for). There is no separate collection, so its Bookings hang off its List id and assignment keeps the id.
  - createDraftList and the recurring clash write through one insertDraftList and leave schedule.slots and every other List untouched; prove it with a test.
  - Only assignDraftList puts it in a Slot, through attachListToSlot, in the session its day and session fix (the admin chooses only the anaesthetist), in one commit with a draftList.assign meta; the draft trail is kept with assignedAtISO. Then Phase 27's syncPrepayment (cause listMoved) runs for its Bookings; 15a's warnings are derived on read (store/warnings.ts), so they need no call, but their rules and OpenWarningRow must tolerate a Booking on a Draft List. A Booking on a Draft List has no anaesthetist yet, so syncPrepayment must generate and withdraw nothing for it, and a sent prepayment keeps its agreed amount (D20).
  - An assigned List only becomes a Draft List through detachListToDraft, built and unit-tested here for Phase 32 (origins movedToOffice and unavailableReturn); no screen in this phase calls it.
  - removeDraftList soft-removes and refuses while it holds an active Booking; redateDraftList moves it and its Bookings to another day and keeps its waiting time.
  - A Draft List cannot be submitted, authorised or billed, and an anaesthetist cannot add a Booking to one.
  - No projection, roll forward or new-anaesthetist path may overwrite a List id a Draft List holds, and a recurring booking never projects a second List or Draft List for a day it already answered for (the Draft List keeps recurringBookingId, and a recurring clash keeps the day in draft.projectedFor even after a re-date or a removal).
- The recurring clash (OQ-81 part 2, built as the answer): one pure recurringClashDraft turns each of Phase 30's skipped sessions (a recurring booking covering a closed session) into a Draft List with the recurring booking's hospital, surgeon, kind and notes, origin recurringClash and a stable derived id. It runs on every path that applies the projection: addRecurringBooking, editRecurringBooking, applyRecurringBookingsToCanvas ("Apply to canvas now"), every roll forward, the horizon extend, and the seed's generation. Phase 29 planned paintSeriesOnNewSlots to run after generateCanvasForDates, which keeps and flags a recurring-booking List on a series-closed new Slot: paint the series first (or replace that flag with the Draft List), so no recurring booking is ever left flagged on the anaesthetist (work item 9). Never for a past day. It writes no availability conflict and never shows on Conflicts for the anaesthetist (US-01.5.4 AC3); a hospital closure still raises Phase 30's holiday conflict. An edit, retire or move of the recurring booking updates or removes an empty clash Draft List and keeps one with Bookings. Phase 30's sheet wording for skipped sessions now says they go to Draft Lists.

Explicit save and the update email

Intake After phases 17, 25, 32, 33 2 sessions plan doc ↗ 7 items covered

Admin edits a Booking in a draft and saves it explicitly. Each save is one change set, with grouped history and an as-at view, and the office can edit every field. An on-demand update email on any Admin Booking, the List drawer or a List-move notification lets the office pick changes from the history and opens a mailto from a per-kind template, to the rooms or the hospital. A Booking can be added to a booked List. Anaesthetists keep immediate saves.

DM-35RV-31FT-02.3boardUS-02.3.1boardUS-02.3.2boardUS-02.3.3boardUS-02.3.4board

Open questions: OQ-82

Demo triggers and risks
  • Admin Booking detail: 'Draft update email' with the change picker and a badged preview panel alongside the real mailto (product)
  • Admin notification pool: 'Draft cover-change email' on a List-move notification (product)
  • Admin Master data, Email templates: edit a template, then draft an email of that kind (product)
  • PWA sheet, mobile Booking: 'Office edits this Booking' (a saved office change arrives on the handset)

Risks. The shared Booking detail must keep the mobile and web immediate-save paths intact: draft-then-save is office-only. Whether a List reassignment is itself a save is left open by the catalogue: treat it as its own history entry the email can pick. Whether an anaesthetist's own move should email automatically is OQ-82: build on demand only. This supersedes, for the office, the 2026-07-23 'write-through per tap' ruling: record it. S5 Beat 1 audit gains change sets.

- Draft-then-save is Admin only. Mobile, web and the PWA mount no draft provider and keep their immediate saves exactly as today; the anaesthetist never calls saveBookingChanges.
- Nothing on the Admin Booking detail may bypass the draft. Drafted edits go through the booking-store context; commands (complete, uncomplete, cancel, move, the prepayment, event and invoice actions where built, and the update email) act on the real store and are disabled while there are unsaved changes. A drafted action may touch only the snapshot's slices and never emit an app event (the emitter is shared by every store); a demo Reset discards a dirty draft. Add the source-scanning test that enforces it. In draft mode, sheet buttons read Apply, not Save.
- One save is one change set: one change-set id across the entries, a booking.save header, the office as the actor. The lastModified stamps never appear in audit before or after. A save applies the admin's own changes onto the real Booking as it is at Save time, reading each before value from it; a cancel, move or authorise in between blocks it with a plain reason. No row versions, merge or clash prompt: concurrent edits (US-02.5.6) are Future Work. Remap draft-created ids against the real counters and re-check the existing invariants (22's split-share validation, one primary Procedure, Contract eligibility, validateNhi). A save runs 27's syncPrepayment once on the real store; in the draft store it is a no-op.
- Every List owner change (28's reassignment, 31's assignment, 32's moves, whichever app makes them) carries a listReassign change set and shows in the History of the List's Bookings; a List reassignment is its own event, not a save, and its flow keeps no email step (US-01.4.1).
- The office can edit every field of a Booking (US-02.3.1's note): add the NHI to the office's Edit patient sheet (validateNhi), let the office edit the procedure description on a SUBMITTED List, give the time a proper field, and open up any other field the drift check found or record why not. AUTHORISED stays read-only.
- Keep the change-set maths, the as-at reconstruction, the template validation and rendering, and the email builder and picker pure, in src/domain, with Vitest tests. Order as-at by audit sequence, not time (the demo clock has minute resolution).
- The email is a real mailto link, on demand only: a Draft update email button on every Admin Booking and in the List drawer, and Draft cover-change email on a List-move notification in 32's pool; never a prompt after a save, a reassignment or an assignment, and never sent automatically. The admin picks one or more rows from the history (saves, creations, cancellations, moves, applied hospital rows, coalesced anaesthetist edits, cover changes); only those appear, netted per field. It starts from the admin-maintained template for the kind of change (Change of anaesthetist, Cancellation, Correction of an error, Booking change), editable in Master data. Opening the mail client writes one "Update email drafted (not sent)" entry and nothing else; nothing is stored or labelled as sent. The whole encoded link is at most 2,000 characters (one labelled constant), and a shortened body says so. Only the allowlisted fields appear: never an NHI, date of birth, internal notes, Contract, payer details or money, and a List email names no patient. A single-Booking move (32a, if DONE) is a Booking change for the rooms with the new anaesthetist on its line, not a cover change (OQ-46: a new anaesthetist on a List); 32a's handoff reads it as a cover change, so log the reading for the owner.
- Migrate the framed build's router to a data router for useBlocker, keeping every URL and Playwright entry point; leave pwa/main.tsx alone. Run npm run shots straight after the migration.
- Determinism: no Date.now(), new Date() or Math.random(). Seed the four templates in the seed builders, leave the canvas generator untouched, and bump PERSIST_VERSION by one.
- Saves that do not come from the Admin draft (the S5 jump and the PWA trigger) go through the saveBookingPatch convenience over saveBookingChanges, never hand-built snapshots.
- Demo triggers go into Phase 14's registry, never the Control Panel page: "Office edits this Booking" on the mobile Booking (PWA only, office stand-in badge), and an Admin "An anaesthetist moves this List to a colleague" trigger only if 32 shipped none. The update email, the composer's badged preview panel and the template editor are product actions.
- Keep S2 intact: phone advice on a free session and its isScriptedS2Booking prefill still work, the Beat 3 reassignment ends as before, and 32's own-move beat gains the pool's cover-change email. Add Booking (the control 31 put on the Draft List drawer) also works on a booked List.
- Design: teal is the only action colour and crimson never appears on the new surfaces; warning tint for unsaved, success tint for saved, neutral for notices; Admin overlays through useSurface().Overlay; proper desktop layout. No en or em dashes in any app copy, seeded template, email text or trigger label, and never "slot" in app copy.

Net per anaesthetist is never below zero; what a run cannot net stays open on the negative invoice and nets in a later run with positives. An anaesthetist with only negatives is not in a run. The offset is its own amount on the payable leg (offsetAmount), never counted as cash, and the whole ledger stays in balance after approval, sending and detection.

Pre-op and post-op events

Capture After phases 24, NaN 2 sessions plan doc ↗ 5 items covered

Anaesthetist and office add pre-op and post-op events on a Procedure (time or fixed fee, invoice tick, "same as" party). An event goes on the Procedure's invoice before approval, or its own invoice in the next run after it, with one review step. ACC pre-op becomes a fixed-fee event. Billing lines get a date, preset types, Contract add-ons and UNIT x RATE.

Demo triggers and risks
  • Mobile and web Procedure: 'Add pre-op or post-op event' (product), on a past billed Procedure of Dr Souter's that the re-pointed 'Stage post-op scenario' provides, and on a current Procedure before its List is authorised
  • Mobile and web Procedure: 'Add billing line' with a preset type, a UNIT x RATE line or a Contract add-on fee, dated days after the procedure (product)
  • Admin review of events: the standard review step, then the next billing run (product)

Risks. It needs nothing from 39 or 39a, so it may run straight after 38b to restore the anaesthetist's late-charge path sooner. Greg was unconvinced by the name 'event': keep the user-facing name in 38b's one label. The 'same as' default is our reading: label it. An event billed to another party cannot ride on the Procedure's invoice, so it gets its own (our reading of 'if possible'). The ACC codes are OQ-12 (AA's accountant): label them provisional. Whether the Contract defined rate also prices a line outside BTM is OQ-89: the UNIT x RATE line calls Phase 24's rate function and adds no pricing of its own. Whether post-op reviews leave the billing-line list for events is not stated: offer both. A refund shown as an event is tentative: do not build. Re-point 'Stage post-op scenario' to Dr Souter, the only anaesthetist persona. The fee stays hidden on the anaesthetist side. Mobile-first: bottom sheets, not desktop forms. An event's own invoice is its own BCTI and feeds Phase 16's count function.

Owing within the threshold is a mild (yellow) warning (the 30-day case is mild, not silent); strictly older than the threshold is strong (red); a credit held for the patient with nothing owing is mild; the age counts from the invoice date in one function (invoiceAgeDays). A cancel is never refused because of a prepayment. Only cancellation refunds are paid out of the trust account; 39's credit note option pays no refund (US-08.6.5).
- The rebook is for a true cancellation only. It creates a new Booking through createBooking (Copy a Booking is gone) and lets Phase 27's engine generate the fresh prepayment at the replacement's unit value, held for Approve and send. Nothing moves between anaesthetists.
- Letters are plain-text templates with a fixed estimate notice the template cannot remove (it promises no refund), rendered when an admin approves and sends and snapshotted on the invoice, with no NHI. The letter-merge maths, the settlement unit value and the trust view are pure in src/domain/billing with Vitest tests; names come from src/shared/format.ts.
- Every mutation goes through mutate() with audit and the right actor. Refunds, payouts, reminders, rebooks and template edits are office only; the release runs as the billing run and the payable update as the billing engine; the bank settles a payout as a system actor. Time comes from the demo clock: no Date.now(), new Date() or Math.random().
- Keep the filler generator's rng() draw order unchanged and bump PERSIST_VERSION once per session that changes the seed.
- Mobile uses bottom sheets, web and admin use dialogs, and teal is the only action colour. Crimson never appears on the letter, the refund section, the trust tiles or any button. Amounts and numbers are in mono with tabular-nums. No en or em dashes in app copy or seeded template text; say "move", never "swap", and never "slot" in app copy.
- Demo triggers go in the Phase 14 registry only, never on the Control Panel page. The bar gets "Stage overpaid prepayment" on Admin Review and "Pay out trust refund" on the Xero sim. The PWA gets the office stand-ins "Office sends a pre-payment reminder" and "Office refunds this pre-payment from the trust account" on the mobile Booking (badged office stand-in, as OFFICE_SIMULATION_ACTOR). The letter picker, reminder, move lines, refund, payout, rebook and template actions are product UI, unbadged. Bodies live in src/shared or src/store so pwaPurity passes.
- Do not commit or push.

Scale and privacy

NFR After phases 34, 36, 37, 42 1 session plan doc ↗ 2 items covered

Scale: a 'Load full-scale data' demo action (Admin Day and Invoices, with a confirm step) builds the whole practice in memory from the seed. That is 85 anaesthetists (14 demo anaesthetists unchanged plus 71 generated), Slots across Phase 28's horizon setting (about 21,000 at four months, called 'sessions' in the UI, never 'slot'), and about 28,000 invoices over 12 months through the real billing and ledger builders. It includes a review backlog and a handful of Billing monitor problems. Saving pauses and nothing is serialised. A banner shows generation and per-screen timings at demo and full scale. Admin Day, Invoices, Audit, the Ledger and Phase 37's restyled Billing monitor (US-13.3.1) page, sort and filter at scale. Reset or reload returns to the seed. Privacy: the matching screen shows only the mapped fields. A restricted 'View raw row' is office only, needs a reason, is audited and masked, and a harness entry shows another role refused. Diagnostics are redacted. A Data Inspector 'Scan for NHI leaks' covers Xero (NHI and personal information, OQ-30), logs, refusals and failure reasons, with a planted-leak proof. A neutral 'Synthetic data only' badge shows everywhere.

US-15.0.4boardUS-15.0.6board
Demo triggers and risks
  • Admin Day and Invoices: 'Load full-scale data'
  • Data Inspector: 'Scan for NHI leaks'
  • Matching screen, selected unmatched row (context hook): 'View raw row' (office only, reason required, audited)

Parked

In scope, but deliberately not planned yet.

Milestones

What a workshop can be shown once each milestone phase is done.

  • After phase 16
    Booking vocabulary everywhere, with Copy a Booking gone and photo capture out of the Add a booking chooser (15b). Every demo action on its own screen, in the harness bar and on a handset, with the HL7/FHIR tooling badged Future scope. Warnings, never blocks (15a): one routine, the to-do list, a triangle on Bookings and a warning clear on opening, the prepayment gate turned into a warning, and no confirm step at submit. The corrected payables story: the payable equals the receivable, AA's fee is a monthly invoice built from its settings, and Xero holds no patient names.
  • After phase 25
    The catalogue's pricing model end to end: editable RVG reference, modifier and master procedure lists, with default modifiers pre-filled and untickable; base units from each procedure's default RVG Contract with Contract overrides, any value accepted and an office warning when out of range; a procedure-first pick, then one Contract per Procedure filtered by procedure then hospital, with the default RVG Contract always offered and code search; the billable party defined by the Contract, with the payer's name and email captured on a default Contract, required inputs and a child warning; invoices sent by the billing run, with full or split payment and typed $ or % shares; the 3/2/2 modifier split, combination Contracts, the Contract defined unit rate and a Contract-gated adjustment; and a lock at AUTHORISED that reproduces invoices exactly. S3, S4 Beat 3 and S5 are re-scripted.
  • After phase 27
    Prepayment from the anaesthetist's prepaid set for a person paying for the patient: the estimate from estimated duration with RVG time rounding and contingency units, worded as an estimate, the invoice generated at setup and sent on admin approval, part-paid tracking, a warning in both apps that strengthens as the date nears, and a prepaid amount above the final billed with no failure. S4 Beat 1 is re-scripted.
  • After phase 32a
    The office's schedule: every session stored and free by default over a configurable horizon, Slots and Lists, statuses as a user-maintained list, the availability calendar with series, the conflict dashboard, Draft Lists that hold Bookings with a waiting flag (including from a recurring clash), blacklist warnings, anaesthetists returning or handing on their own Lists (also when they mark a booked session unavailable) and moving single Bookings, and the office's shared notification pool. S2 is re-scripted.
  • After phase 35
    S1 rebuilt: hospital sync, then the matching screen, then a Booking on its default Contract. Explicit save with change sets, and the on-demand update email picked from the change history, started from a template, to the rooms or the hospital, including from a List-move notification.
  • After phase 39a
    The money story on the internal ledger: balances shown in or out of balance, Xero mirror resilience and a processing monitor grouped by anaesthetist with sorting and filters, ledger-backed web accounts with a flat outstanding list and a cash-basis GST schedule, events on a Procedure with the events list and free-form additional invoices to any party (38b), the credit note option, credit-and-rebill from copied lines and a split combined procedure, and payment runs with BCTI approval, netting and a remittance advice. S4 Beats 2 to 5 are re-scripted.
  • After phase 44
    Every verified gap closed: finding past work, pre-op and post-op events on every Procedure, patients with balance warnings, follow-up tools and NHI lookup, prepayment letters, settlement, the trust account and refunds, reference-data loads, full-scale and privacy demos, anaesthetist sign-in, point-of-need help, and the rewritten S1 to S5 run sheet.
